svg.title: The hydrologic cycle, redrawn after Horton (1931)
svg.desc: Line drawing: a cross-section from the sea to a hillside. Water evaporates from the sea, is carried inland as cloud, falls as rain on trees and fields, soaks into the soil or runs off downhill, and returns to the sea through streams and ground water. Thirteen numbered steps are listed below.

g.text: redrawn after Robert E. Horton, 1931, p. 193
Water leaves the sea as vapour, falls as
rain, and splits at the ground: part soaks
in, part runs off, part goes back to the
air. Nothing in this diagram belongs

svg.text: the same numbers mark where the hail cannon and the tiemperos act
the sun lifts water vapour off the sea
wind moves the vapour over the land
rising air cools and the vapour becomes cloud
rain, hail or snow falls from the cloud
leaves and crops catch part of the rain
plants return water to the air through leaves
soil, ponds and puddles dry under the sun
rain soaks in through the ground surface
what cannot soak in flows downhill over the ground
water held in the soil, where roots take it up
water drains deeper, down to the water table
slow flow underground to springs, streams, the sea
channels carry the water back to the sea
Wording and layout are new; check the terms against Horton’s original figure.
